parity_risks.note: The Sort is not cosmetic: tools 5, 6, 7 and 9 all read its row order, which is why the segmenter kept 4-9 together. NULL sorts first ascending and last descending, so every window's ORDER BY spells the NULLS placement out.

Unique keeps the FIRST row of each (ACCT, POSTED_DT) in incoming order, and incoming order is the Sort's ENTRY_ID DESC, so the surviving duplicate is the one with the LARGEST ENTRY_ID. A row number taken in any other order changes which row's AMOUNT reaches the Summarize.
Unique compares key values exactly, and two NULL POSTED_DT rows of the same ACCT count as the same key. PARTITION BY treats NULLs as one group, which is the same rule.

RUN_BAL is a Double field, so the model adds the exact decimal amounts and converts to a binary double when it stores each row. The translation sums the NUMBER column in a window and casts once, which agrees for every amount in the golden sets; a running total long enough to lose a double's precision would not.

Record ID numbers rows in incoming order, so its value depends entirely on the Sort. It never reaches the target -- the Summarize drops it -- but CLOSING_BAL is defined as the last row by that number, so ordering.order_dependent_columns names CLOSING_BAL.
IIF's condition is NULL when POSTED_DT is NULL, and a NULL condition takes the else branch in both Alteryx and SQL, so those rows are flagged 'N' rather than NULL.
Alteryx's Count counts ROWS, not values, so ENTRIES is COUNT(*) and the edge set's NULL-ENTRY_ID row still counts as one.

Last takes the group's last row in incoming order, including a NULL. There is no ordered aggregate for it in either dialect, so the translation takes the value at the largest RECORD_ID; that is the same row as long as RECORD_ID is unique, which it is because it is a row number.

Update; Insert if new maps columns to the target by NAME and writes only the six the Summarize produces. LOADED_FLAG is left untouched on a matched row and arrives NULL on an inserted one, which is precisely what the PostSQL then fills. A NULL update key matches nothing, so the edge set's NULL-ACCT group is inserted rather than merged.

The golden output is the target's state AFTER PreSQL, write and PostSQL -- not this run's rows. A row the run does not touch (9999) stays exactly as it was, and PERIOD < '2020-01' is deleted before anything is written.
